answer: Each identity must gather attestation from node clusters that share no operator, forming a quorum no single actor can forge alone. A cipher key tied to one cluster cannot vouch for a second cluster, so an attacker renting a zephyr of cheap VPS still needs operators outside its own network to sign. Minting a fresh plume of accounts multiplies the number of independent clusters that must agree, and that agreement cannot be bought in bulk from one source, so cost rises per head instead of falling with scale.
